Skill loaded successfully ✅

# 2D&D Game Development

Start with [`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md), then use
[`docs/architecture.md`](../../../docs/architecture.md) and
[`docs/development.md`](../../../docs/development.md) for current ownership and
workflow.

Use this skill for cross-cutting game features, new content, combat behavior,
and changes spanning scenes, systems, data, renderers, or managers.

## Core rules

1. Use strict TypeScript with explicit parameter and return types.
2. Keep content data-driven in `src/data/`; keep reusable logic in
   `src/systems/`.
3. Generate reusable textures in `src/renderers/textures.ts`; scene-sized
   procedural Battle scenery belongs in `battleBackdrop.ts`. Synthesize audio
   in `src/systems/audio.ts`; do not add external assets.
4. Preserve shared scene state across transitions.
5. Use `debugLog()` and debug-panel APIs instead of `console.log`.
6. Add deterministic Vitest coverage for game logic.

## Current architecture

- Phaser 4 scenes: `Boot`, `Overworld`, `Battle`, `Shop`, `Codex`, `Cutscene`,
  `Ending`, and `Defeat`
- Overworld orchestration: `src/scenes/Overworld.ts`
- Battle orchestration: `src/scenes/Battle.ts`
- Core mechanics: `src/systems/`
- Immutable definitions: `src/data/`
- Extracted presentation: `src/renderers/`
- Battle environment composition: `src/renderers/battleBackdrop.ts`
- Shared Battle depth contract: `src/renderers/battleDepth.ts`
- Stateful scene helpers: `src/managers/`
- Shared audio/accessibility preferences: `src/systems/accessibility.ts`
- Typed semantic actions and state: `src/systems/input.ts`
- Keyboard/pointer/gamepad/touch adapter: `src/managers/input.ts`

The versioned `2dnd_preferences` document is separate from campaign saves and
backs both title and in-game settings. Install the scene accessibility adapter
in every scene, use its shared reduced-motion accessors, preserve
100%/125%/150% text usability, and pair important color states with a textual or
symbolic cue. Control presentation preferences cover touch visibility,
handedness, and prompt source without changing campaign saves. Stable mappings
are intentionally not remappable.

All release input routes through the semantic action layer. Standard gamepads
use dead zones, digital fallback, repeat/debounce, source switching, and a
visible right-stick cursor clicked by pressing the stick. Responsive touch controls use safe areas, pointer
capture for held directions, click pulses for discrete actions, and mobile text
entry. Clear held state on blur, visibility loss, disconnect, scene changes,
and shutdown.

Cutscene contracts live in `src/data/cutsceneTypes.ts`, focused campaign and
boss definitions live in `cutsceneCampaign.ts` and `cutsceneBosses.ts`, and
`src/data/cutscenes.ts` is the stable-ID hub. Pure trigger snapshots, priority
ordering, queue lifecycle, recovery, Chronicle selection, and summary logic live
in `src/systems/cutscenes.ts`; `src/managers/cutscene.ts` owns step progression;
scenes and renderers own input and presentation.
Hero-role actors remain immutable staging cues and resolve at presentation time
from the current `PlayerState`. Build the canonical descriptor with
`src/systems/heroVisuals.ts` and acquire cleanup-safe procedural textures through
`src/renderers/heroTextures.ts`; do not duplicate class, appearance, equipment
layer, fallback, or cache-key rules in Cutscene, Overworld, Battle, or Ending.
`EndingScene` and `DefeatScene` share `src/renderers/result.ts`; defeat receives
an exact runtime-only `PartyDefeatResult`, while the recovered player state is
autosaved before presentation.

The map hub is `src/data/map.ts`; terrain/types, chunks, cities, and dungeons
are split into dedicated modules. Dungeon trap definitions live in
`src/data/traps.ts`, mechanics in `src/systems/traps.ts`, and scene orchestration
in `src/managers/dungeonTraps.ts`.
Group templates live in `src/data/monsterGroups.ts`; reusable initiative,
formation, synergy, reward, and per-combatant rules live in
`src/systems/groupCombat.ts`.
That module also owns party-ready `BattleCombatantState`, stable actor IDs,
actor-ID initiative, ally/enemy targeting, monster party-target selection, and
battle resolution hooks.
`src/systems/battleActions.ts` is the Phaser-free action planner for player
input and ranked gambits: actor enumeration, target binding, validation,
immutable plans, per-actor action/bonus consumption, and one-action dispatch.
`executeValidatedBattleAction()` binds a generic `CombatActorState` to a party
combatant and reuses existing attack, spell, ability, item, defend, element,
status, MP, and inventory mechanics.
Consumables consume the acting source's inventory while applying HP/MP/cures
to a selected ally source; execution contexts must include all party action
sources. Equipment actions remain self-targeted.

`src/systems/animation.ts` is the Phaser-free presentation contract for actor
states, deterministic timing, stable-ID target mapping, once-only lifecycle,
and explicit family/frame texture metadata. `src/managers/actorAnimation.ts`
owns reusable Phaser poses and cleanup; battle/world directors consume resolved
state without changing mechanics. `src/renderers/actorTextures.ts` supports
optional family frames from #49 and a generic existing-texture fallback.

semantic control actions, categories, and unlock requirements.

filtering. `src/managers/tutorial.ts` owns the Overworld overlay and renders prompts for

  cities and three keystones, with Ironbound Dispatch, Silk Against the Cold,
  and optional Hydra and Dragon objectives.

  already-completed objectives.

4. Add biome/dungeon tags, encounter weight, and an optional synergy with a

5. Add deterministic generation and data-integrity coverage.

# 2D&D Game Development

Start with [`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md), then use
[`docs/architecture.md`](../../../docs/architecture.md) and
[`docs/development.md`](../../../docs/development.md) for current ownership and
workflow.

Use this skill for cross-cutting game features, new content, combat behavior,
and changes spanning scenes, systems, data, renderers, or managers.

## Core rules

1. Use strict TypeScript with explicit parameter and return types.
2. Keep content data-driven in `src/data/`; keep reusable logic in
   `src/systems/`.
3. Generate reusable textures in `src/renderers/textures.ts`; scene-sized
   procedural Battle scenery belongs in `battleBackdrop.ts`. Synthesize audio
   in `src/systems/audio.ts`; do not add external assets.
4. Preserve shared scene state across transitions.
5. Use `debugLog()` and debug-panel APIs instead of `console.log`.
6. Add deterministic Vitest coverage for game logic.

## Current architecture

- Phaser 4 scenes: `Boot`, `Overworld`, `Battle`, `Shop`, `Codex`, `Cutscene`,
  `Ending`, and `Defeat`
- Overworld orchestration: `src/scenes/Overworld.ts`
- Battle orchestration: `src/scenes/Battle.ts`
- Core mechanics: `src/systems/`
- Immutable definitions: `src/data/`
- Extracted presentation: `src/renderers/`
- Battle environment composition: `src/renderers/battleBackdrop.ts`
- Shared Battle depth contract: `src/renderers/battleDepth.ts`
- Stateful scene helpers: `src/managers/`
- Shared audio/accessibility preferences: `src/systems/accessibility.ts`
- Typed semantic actions and state: `src/systems/input.ts`
- Keyboard/pointer/gamepad/touch adapter: `src/managers/input.ts`

The versioned `2dnd_preferences` document is separate from campaign saves and
backs both title and in-game settings. Install the scene accessibility adapter
in every scene, use its shared reduced-motion accessors, preserve
100%/125%/150% text usability, and pair important color states with a textual or
symbolic cue. Control presentation preferences cover touch visibility,
handedness, and prompt source without changing campaign saves. Stable mappings
are intentionally not remappable.

All release input routes through the semantic action layer. Standard gamepads
use dead zones, digital fallback, repeat/debounce, source switching, and a
visible right-stick cursor clicked by pressing the stick. Responsive touch controls use safe areas, pointer
capture for held directions, click pulses for discrete actions, and mobile text
entry. Clear held state on blur, visibility loss, disconnect, scene changes,
and shutdown.

Cutscene contracts live in `src/data/cutsceneTypes.ts`, focused campaign and
boss definitions live in `cutsceneCampaign.ts` and `cutsceneBosses.ts`, and
`src/data/cutscenes.ts` is the stable-ID hub. Pure trigger snapshots, priority
ordering, queue lifecycle, recovery, Chronicle selection, and summary logic live
in `src/systems/cutscenes.ts`; `src/managers/cutscene.ts` owns step progression;
scenes and renderers own input and presentation.
Hero-role actors remain immutable staging cues and resolve at presentation time
from the current `PlayerState`. Build the canonical descriptor with
`src/systems/heroVisuals.ts` and acquire cleanup-safe procedural textures through
`src/renderers/heroTextures.ts`; do not duplicate class, appearance, equipment
layer, fallback, or cache-key rules in Cutscene, Overworld, Battle, or Ending.
`EndingScene` and `DefeatScene` share `src/renderers/result.ts`; defeat receives
an exact runtime-only `PartyDefeatResult`, while the recovered player state is
autosaved before presentation.

The map hub is `src/data/map.ts`; terrain/types, chunks, cities, and dungeons
are split into dedicated modules. Dungeon trap definitions live in
`src/data/traps.ts`, mechanics in `src/systems/traps.ts`, and scene orchestration
in `src/managers/dungeonTraps.ts`.
Group templates live in `src/data/monsterGroups.ts`; reusable initiative,
formation, synergy, reward, and per-combatant rules live in
`src/systems/groupCombat.ts`.
That module also owns party-ready `BattleCombatantState`, stable actor IDs,
actor-ID initiative, ally/enemy targeting, monster party-target selection, and
battle resolution hooks.
`src/systems/battleActions.ts` is the Phaser-free action planner for player
input and ranked gambits: actor enumeration, target binding, validation,
immutable plans, per-actor action/bonus consumption, and one-action dispatch.
`executeValidatedBattleAction()` binds a generic `CombatActorState` to a party
combatant and reuses existing attack, spell, ability, item, defend, element,
status, MP, and inventory mechanics.
Consumables consume the acting source's inventory while applying HP/MP/cures
to a selected ally source; execution contexts must include all party action
sources. Equipment actions remain self-targeted.

`src/systems/animation.ts` is the Phaser-free presentation contract for actor
states, deterministic timing, stable-ID target mapping, once-only lifecycle,
and explicit family/frame texture metadata. `src/managers/actorAnimation.ts`
owns reusable Phaser poses and cleanup; battle/world directors consume resolved
state without changing mechanics. `src/renderers/actorTextures.ts` supports
optional family frames from #49 and a generic existing-texture fallback.

Tutorial and Tips content lives in `src/data/tutorial.ts` as immutable steps,
semantic control actions, categories, and unlock requirements.
`src/systems/tutorial.ts` owns completion normalization and progression-aware
filtering. `src/managers/tutorial.ts` owns the Overworld overlay and renders prompts for
the active keyboard, pointer, gamepad, or touch source. New saves persist
`player.progression.tutorial.completed`; replay never resets it.

Progressive feature discovery is data-driven through
`src/data/featureDiscovery.ts` and `src/systems/featureDiscovery.ts`. Filter
menus, tabs, shortcuts, prompts, touch actions, and Codex/crafting/gathering
categories through the shared registry. Preserve always-safe Inventory, Map,
Equipment, Tips, Settings, and save/title controls, and never use discovery as
authority for gameplay state.

World Event content lives in `src/data/worldEvents.ts`, its deterministic
Phaser-free state machine in `src/systems/worldEvents.ts`, and accessible choice
presentation in `src/managers/worldEvents.ts`. Events short-circuit treasure,
exploration checks, and random encounters for their movement step, while
transitions, entrances, traps, interactions, and queued cutscenes retain
priority. Special event combats use normal Battle hooks and saves.

## Quests

- Put quest definitions, stage objectives, NPC IDs, rewards, and gated
  entrances in `src/data/quests.ts`.
- Put progression, normalization, idempotent rewards, NPC interaction
  resolution, journal entries, and entrance checks behind
  `src/systems/quests.ts`; `questState.ts` and `questDebug.ts` contain focused
  normalization and debug-only mutation helpers.
- Persist state only through `player.progression.quests`; use quest-system APIs
  instead of direct mutation.
- The shipped campaign is the seven-chapter Twelvefold Covenant across all 12
  cities and three keystones, with Ironbound Dispatch, Silk Against the Cold,
  and optional Hydra and Dragon objectives.
- Persist objective counters and claimed reward IDs. Batch group defeats with
  duplicate monster IDs intact so three matching combatants count as three.
- Downstream unlocks such as companions should call `isQuestCompleted()` and
  keep their own persistent state separate from quest reward bookkeeping.
- Cross-system outcomes use stable quest completion actions with
  `{ id, type, targetId }`. Replay them after load/mutations and make the
  consumer idempotent rather than adding duplicate quest state.
- Give every stage a stable camelCase `id`; downstream systems use
  `getQuestStageIndex()` or the debug-only `setQuestStageById()`, never display
  titles.
- Derive boss objectives from `defeatedBosses` so older saves can report
  already-completed objectives.
- Keep quest NPCs available at night and test every referenced NPC, boss,
  reward item, and entrance.
- Campaign completion remains derived from the main quest. Launch the epilogue
  after the final Elowen dialogue applies rewards, recover completed-but-unseen
  saves from Overworld creation, and keep replay presentation-only.
- Queue stable cutscene IDs and save before presentation. Completion or skip
  moves an ID from `pendingCutsceneIds` to `seenCutsceneIds`; reload resumes the
  first pending entry, while Chronicle replay changes neither collection.
- Detect newly satisfied cutscenes by comparing immutable before/after snapshots.
  Battle must capture its snapshot before recording the defeated boss. Sort
  simultaneous triggers by explicit numeric priority rather than discovery
  order.
- Map main-quest talk objectives through `QUEST_NPCS` and assert exact coverage
  of all 12 live city IDs; do not accept name-only references.
- Canyonwatch, Ashfall, and the Volcanic Forge are hard gates. Sandport and
  Heartlands Crypt remain open; other premature travel uses one-time soft
  danger warnings and capped encounter modifiers.

## Non-combat skill checks

Non-combat checks are split across:

- `src/data/skillChecks.ts`: NPC challenges, negotiation choices, and terrain
  event definitions
- `src/systems/skillChecks.ts`: pure d20 resolution, normalization, and helpers
- `src/managers/skillChecks.ts`: Overworld rewards, hazards, chest checks, and
  dialogue orchestration

## Adding monsters

1. Define the monster in the appropriate focused pool (`monsters.ts`,
   `nightMonsters.ts`, or `monsterVariants.ts`).
2. Use a camelCase ID and set a valid typed `family`, stats, rewards, drops,
   abilities, and `isBoss`.
3. For a palette/stat variant, set `variantOf` to a valid same-family monster,
   use a distinct color and ability set, and assign a positive
   `encounterWeight`.
4. Add an `affinity` and `elementalProfile` when the monster has a dominant
   element, resistances, weaknesses, or
   immunities.
5. Add `element` and `statusEffect` to monster abilities when applicable.
6. Ensure the definition is included in `ALL_MONSTERS`; debug spawning, Codex
   browsing, and ID lookup depend on the master list.
7. Reuse `getMonsterTextureKey()` and the family silhouette renderer rather than
   adding scene-local textures or tints.
8. Add encounter-pool, family, palette, texture-key, and data-integrity tests.

Use `getMonster(id)` for exact ID lookup and `findMonster(query)` for
case-insensitive ID/name lookup with partial matching.

## Adding monster groups

1. Add a 2-4 member template to `MONSTER_GROUP_TEMPLATES`.
2. Reference valid monster IDs and assign every member to `front` or `back`.
3. Keep `minPlayerLevel` high enough that total difficulty does not exceed
   `playerLevel * 3`.
4. Add biome/dungeon tags, encounter weight, and an optional synergy with a
   valid break threshold.
5. Add deterministic generation and data-integrity coverage.

Random groups start at level 2, cap at 50% of triggered encounters, and never
replace bosses or explicit debug monster spawns.

Codex family completion is derived from the current `CodexData.entries`; family
metadata, affinity, and sort/filter presentation are not save fields.

World knowledge definitions live in `src/data/codexKnowledge.ts`. Persist only
stable unlocked knowledge IDs in `CodexData`; derive category counts, source
hints, search results, sorting, and grouping from canonical entries. Emit
idempotent location, quest, cutscene, item, NPC, readable, or `worldEvent`
signals without letting Codex state control gameplay. `reputationMilestone`
is owned by the schema-v12 reputation system and must remain idempotent.

## World Events

- Filter immutable definitions by terrain, area, time, weather, level, quest
  state, boss state, prior outcomes, repeat limits, and cooldowns.
- Keep event chance independently capped at 8%; never feed it into or multiply
  the 15% random-encounter calculation.
- Persist the selected pending event before presenting choices or starting a
  special battle. Reload resumes the same choice or encounter.
- Apply skill outcomes through `rollSkillCheck()`, quest starts through
  `startQuestById()`, rewards through canonical item/XP helpers, and lore through
  `unlockCodexFromFutureSignal()`.
- Resolve stable outcome/reward IDs once, append at most 40 chronological
  records, and expose those records through Chronicle without revealing future
  choices.
- Alignment/reputation hooks are consumed by the centralized social mutation
  API with stable source IDs. World Event state never persists duplicate social
  scores or applied IDs.

## Alignment and reputation

- Keep canonical axes, faction IDs, reputation tiers, and thresholds in
  `src/data/reputation.ts`; reusable mechanics belong in
  `src/systems/reputation.ts`.
- New players begin exactly Chaotic Neutral (`lawChaos: -50`, `goodEvil: 0`).
- Persist only bounded scores, stable applied source IDs, and the bounded
  recent-cause history. Derive names, tiers, pricing, milestones, and ending
  variants.
- Apply social outcomes only for meaningful choices. Never reward routine
  movement, unavoidable combat, or farming.
- Return runtime-only `SocialAchievementHook` values for the achievement
  consumer; do not persist achievements inside the social system.

## Achievements

- Put immutable definitions and cosmetic titles in `src/data/achievements.ts`;
  put normalization, deterministic progress, reconciliation, stable event
  counters, debug exclusion, and title equip rules in
  `src/systems/achievements.ts`.
- Prefer reconciliation from authoritative quest, boss, Codex, exploration,
  trap, skill-check, event, social, party, and inventory state. Add persisted
  counters only for non-reconstructable event history such as battle wins,
  one-hit defeats, and explicit defeat count.
- Achievement state never controls gameplay authority. Titles are
  presentation-only and notices are queued for safe Overworld presentation.

## Adding spells, abilities, and equipment

- Damage sources may declare an `Element` from `src/data/elements.ts`.
- Player abilities may apply `selfEffect` or `targetEffect` IDs defined by
  `src/systems/statusEffects.ts`.
- Monster abilities use `statusEffect` for effects applied to the player.
- Cure consumables declare matching cure data and must be wired through
  `useItem()` without consuming the item when no matching ailment exists.
- Ally-target consumables declare `targetType`; resolve it through
  `getItemTargetType()` so older inventory copies use canonical item metadata.
- Preserve action economy: normal actions end the player turn; bonus-action
  abilities and the first item use do not.

Combat calculation order is:

1. Roll and resolve the attack or save.
2. Apply active-status accuracy, disadvantage, AC, and damage modifiers.
3. Apply elemental immunity, weakness, or resistance to the modified damage.
4. Apply damage and status effects.
5. Report discoveries and combat feedback.

Magic Missile remains auto-hit and does not roll disadvantage.

## Status effects

All definitions and lifecycle helpers live in
`src/systems/statusEffects.ts`. Do not duplicate status logic in data files or
scenes.

- Start of actor turn: tick damage, saving throws, and skip-turn decision.
- End of actor turn: decrement durations and expire effects.
- Apply or refresh through `applyStatusEffect()`.
- Normalize loaded effects through `normalizeActiveEffects()`.
- Clear player and monster effects when leaving Battle; durations are measured
  in combat turns, not overworld steps.

## Elements

Supported elements are Fire, Ice, Lightning, Poison, Necrotic, Radiant,
Thunder, Force, and Psychic.

- Immunity: zero damage
- Weakness: double damage
- Resistance: floor of half damage
- Neutral: unchanged

Record observed non-neutral interactions with `discoverElement()` so the Codex
can persist and display them.

## World features

- Cities may contain connected districts. Always use city chunk helpers rather
  than indexing `city.chunks` directly.
- Dungeons may contain multiple levels. Always use dungeon level and
  connection helpers.
- Dungeon trap layouts are derived from persisted `trapSeed`; never mutate
  dungeon maps or randomize layouts independently in scenes.
- Detected traps block movement until disarmed. Trap triggers must short-circuit
  the normal random-encounter check for that step.
- Use `FogOfWar.exploredKey()` for exploration keys.
- Use `isWalkable()` and `ENCOUNTER_RATES`; do not hardcode terrain behavior.
- Nautical metadata lives in `src/data/nautical.ts`; state normalization,
  ownership, and mechanics live in the focused `nauticalState.ts`,
  `nauticalOwnership.ts`, and `nautical.ts` modules. Preserve all 90 legacy
  chunk IDs and use `s:zoneId,chunkX,chunkY,x,y` for sea fog.
- Merchant routes work before boat ownership. Free sailing requires a
  serviceable active boat, uses canonical Water eligibility, and runs hazards
  before World Events, gathering, and random sea encounters.

## Non-combat skill checks

- Checks use d20 + Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier plus
  typed bonuses against a DC.
- Natural 1 and 20 are not automatic outcomes for ability checks.
- Persist fixed NPC, shop, chest, and treasure results in
  `player.progression.skillChecks`.
- Use stable NPC identities and shop type/coordinate keys rather than array
  indexes.
- Shop negotiation is one attempt per shop; successful discounts restore from
  the saved result.
- Exploration hazard damage is nonlethal and must clamp the player to at least
  1 HP.
- Test roll math, invalid inputs, stable data references, save normalization,
  reward bounds, and nonlethal damage deterministically.

## Scene changes

State-bearing transitions commonly pass:

```typescript
{
  player,
  defeatedBosses,
  codex,
  timeStep,
  weatherState,
  savedSpecialNpcs,
}
```

Battle also receives a `MonsterEncounter` and biome; Shop receives shop/city
context.
Defeat receives the full shared state plus encounter name/type and the exact
applied party defeat receipt. It must not recalculate or reapply penalties.
Future party systems pass accessor-backed `partyCombatants` plus runtime-only
`battleHooks`; do not persist those wrapper objects.
Keep target `init()` contracts and every caller synchronized.

The new-player tutorial opens only after pending opening cutscenes have drained.
`F1` and the Esc menu open the consultable Tips surface. Keep the external HTML
control rail collapsed by default and retain only contextual action prompts in
the game HUD.

Route camera fades and scene handoffs through
`src/managers/sceneTransition.ts`. Call `prepare()` when each scene creates,
wait for fade-complete events, and keep the duration-plus-grace watchdog as a
recovery path only. Restore the outgoing camera before queueing the next scene,
reject duplicate handoffs, and block state-changing Overworld input until the
queued start/restart is processed. Every Overworld restart must include a fresh
`savedSpecialNpcs` snapshot in the shared state payload.
Use the same guarded Battle exit cleanup for victory, flee, and defeat. Defeat
clears transient menus, input, effects, particles, and weather timers before
starting `DefeatScene`, which continues only to Overworld.
- Resolve an action before presenting it. Actor animation may read stable IDs,
  targets, hit/damage/healing, and outcome, but must not spend MP/items/actions,
  apply damage, report results, or control fade-complete scene handoffs.

## Companions and gambits

- Persistent party state lives at `player.party`; do not add a parallel scene
  payload or companion combat model.
- Stable companion IDs are `guardian`, `scout`, and `mystic`.
- Build runtime actors with `createPartyCombatant()` and
  `createBattleActionSource()`.
- Manual turns and ranked gambits both validate/execute through
  `battleActions.ts`; one bonus action may precede or follow one main action.
- Recruitment consumes replayable quest completion actions idempotently.
- Debug quest or companion recruitment must refresh live follower presentation
  immediately after replay.
- Active conscious companions may render as non-blocking followers, but only
  hero movement invokes trap, encounter, gate, and world-interaction logic.
- Keep party UI/followers/battle presentation in focused managers/renderers
  rather than growing the existing oversized scene/overlay files.

## Inventory presentation

- Build immutable views with `src/systems/inventory.ts`; every view entry keeps
  its original inventory index for actions and transfers.
- Never sort the owning inventory array or replace equipment object references.
- Keep sort/filter/search preferences in `2dnd_inventory_prefs`, outside the
  campaign save schema. Recent acquisition is reverse append order.
- Use semantic inventory actions for keyboard, pointer, gamepad, and touch
  controls. `T` remains mount control.
- Generate item visuals procedurally through `src/renderers/itemVisuals.ts`.

## Gathering

Gathering content lives in `src/data/gathering.ts`, deterministic node/table/
minigame logic in `src/systems/gathering.ts`, schema normalization in
`gatheringState.ts`, and accessible Phaser presentation in
`src/managers/gathering.ts`. Persist selected outcomes before play, use safe
location-derived nodes, route guarded finds through normal Battle hooks, and
keep material identity limited to stable `Item.material` recipe-input metadata.

## Crafting

Crafting recipes live in `src/data/crafting.ts`, atomic mechanics and discovery
in `src/systems/crafting.ts`, persistence normalization in `craftingState.ts`,
and accessible Overworld presentation in `src/managers/crafting.ts`. Validate
the selected actor inventory, protected/equipped restrictions, batch, gold,
station, output, and transaction ID before mutation. Equipment upgrades replace
exact equipped object links with canonical outputs. Never pull companion
materials implicitly, reroll a craft, duplicate material identity, or let
recipes/achievements control quests, Codex, access, or rewards.

## Validation

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:browser
npm run build
```

For UI changes, run the committed Playwright flow in headless Chromium. Keep
browser actions synchronized through debug-state transitions, and hold
frame-polled Phaser keys across frames rather than using instantaneous presses.
Build responsive UI from `src/systems/layout.ts`, register modal groups through
`createOverlayContainer()`, and assert the local `#layout-report` reports zero
unintended overlap or clipping at supported text scales.

## Common pitfalls

- Do not mutate shared monster, item, map, city, or dungeon definitions.
- Do not share HP, status, defend, discovery, or drop state between group
  combatants, including duplicate monsters.
- Do not introduce index-based turn entries or duplicate hero HP/effect state;
  use stable combatant IDs and `createHeroCombatant()`.
- Do not reimplement MP, inventory, target, formation, or action-economy checks
  in companion AI; use `validateBattleAction()`.
- Do not use stale Phaser 3 APIs or default imports; current code uses
  `import * as Phaser from "phaser"`.
- Do not create a second status or elemental calculation path.
- Do not omit unique dungeon pools or bosses from aggregate lookups.
- Do not use geometry masks for the Battle log; render the bounded visible
  message window.
- Do not add a persistent field without save normalization and tests.
- Do not reroll a failed trap detection; persist the `missed` state.

`src/data/featureDiscovery.ts` and `src/systems/featureDiscovery.ts`. Filter
menus, tabs, shortcuts, prompts, touch actions, and Codex/crafting/gathering
categories through the shared registry. Preserve always-safe Inventory, Map,
Equipment, Tips, Settings, and save/title controls, and never use discovery as
authority for gameplay state.

World Event content lives in `src/data/worldEvents.ts`, its deterministic
Phaser-free state machine in `src/systems/worldEvents.ts`, and accessible choice
presentation in `src/managers/worldEvents.ts`. Events short-circuit treasure,
exploration checks, and random encounters for their movement step, while
transitions, entrances, traps, interactions, and queued cutscenes retain
priority. Special event combats use normal Battle hooks and saves.

## Quests

- Put quest definitions, stage objectives, NPC IDs, rewards, and gated
  entrances in `src/data/quests.ts`.
- Put progression, normalization, idempotent rewards, NPC interaction
  resolution, journal entries, and entrance checks behind
  `src/systems/quests.ts`; `questState.ts` and `questDebug.ts` contain focused
  normalization and debug-only mutation helpers.
- Persist state only through `player.progression.quests`; use quest-system APIs
  instead of direct mutation.
- The shipped campaign is the seven-chapter Twelvefold Covenant across all 12
  cities and three keystones, with Ironbound Dispatch, Silk Against the Cold,
  and optional Hydra and Dragon objectives.
- Persist objective counters and claimed reward IDs. Batch group defeats with
  duplicate monster IDs intact so three matching combatants count as three.
- Downstream unlocks such as companions should call `isQuestCompleted()` and
  keep their own persistent state separate from quest reward bookkeeping.
- Cross-system outcomes use stable quest completion actions with
  `{ id, type, targetId }`. Replay them after load/mutations and make the
  consumer idempotent rather than adding duplicate quest state.
- Give every stage a stable camelCase `id`; downstream systems use
  `getQuestStageIndex()` or the debug-only `setQuestStageById()`, never display
  titles.
- Derive boss objectives from `defeatedBosses` so older saves can report
  already-completed objectives.
- Keep quest NPCs available at night and test every referenced NPC, boss,
  reward item, and entrance.
- Campaign completion remains derived from the main quest. Launch the epilogue
  after the final Elowen dialogue applies rewards, recover completed-but-unseen
  saves from Overworld creation, and keep replay presentation-only.
- Queue stable cutscene IDs and save before presentation. Completion or skip
  moves an ID from `pendingCutsceneIds` to `seenCutsceneIds`; reload resumes the
  first pending entry, while Chronicle replay changes neither collection.
- Detect newly satisfied cutscenes by comparing immutable before/after snapshots.
  Battle must capture its snapshot before recording the defeated boss. Sort
  simultaneous triggers by explicit numeric priority rather than discovery
  order.
- Map main-quest talk objectives through `QUEST_NPCS` and assert exact coverage
  of all 12 live city IDs; do not accept name-only references.
- Canyonwatch, Ashfall, and the Volcanic Forge are hard gates. Sandport and
  Heartlands Crypt remain open; other premature travel uses one-time soft
  danger warnings and capped encounter modifiers.

## Non-combat skill checks

Non-combat checks are split across:

- `src/data/skillChecks.ts`: NPC challenges, negotiation choices, and terrain
  event definitions
- `src/systems/skillChecks.ts`: pure d20 resolution, normalization, and helpers
- `src/managers/skillChecks.ts`: Overworld rewards, hazards, chest checks, and
  dialogue orchestration

## Adding monsters

1. Define the monster in the appropriate focused pool (`monsters.ts`,
   `nightMonsters.ts`, or `monsterVariants.ts`).
2. Use a camelCase ID and set a valid typed `family`, stats, rewards, drops,
   abilities, and `isBoss`.
3. For a palette/stat variant, set `variantOf` to a valid same-family monster,
   use a distinct color and ability set, and assign a positive
   `encounterWeight`.
4. Add an `affinity` and `elementalProfile` when the monster has a dominant
   element, resistances, weaknesses, or
   immunities.
5. Add `element` and `statusEffect` to monster abilities when applicable.
6. Ensure the definition is included in `ALL_MONSTERS`; debug spawning, Codex
   browsing, and ID lookup depend on the master list.
7. Reuse `getMonsterTextureKey()` and the family silhouette renderer rather than
   adding scene-local textures or tints.
8. Add encounter-pool, family, palette, texture-key, and data-integrity tests.

Use `getMonster(id)` for exact ID lookup and `findMonster(query)` for
case-insensitive ID/name lookup with partial matching.

## Adding monster groups

1. Add a 2-4 member template to `MONSTER_GROUP_TEMPLATES`.
2. Reference valid monster IDs and assign every member to `front` or `back`.
3. Keep `minPlayerLevel` high enough that total difficulty does not exceed
   `playerLevel * 3`.
4. Add biome/dungeon tags, encounter weight, and an optional synergy with a
   valid break threshold.
5. Add deterministic generation and data-integrity coverage.

Random groups start at level 2, cap at 50% of triggered encounters, and never
replace bosses or explicit debug monster spawns.

Codex family completion is derived from the current `CodexData.entries`; family
metadata, affinity, and sort/filter presentation are not save fields.

World knowledge definitions live in `src/data/codexKnowledge.ts`. Persist only
stable unlocked knowledge IDs in `CodexData`; derive category counts, source
hints, search results, sorting, and grouping from canonical entries. Emit
idempotent location, quest, cutscene, item, NPC, readable, or `worldEvent`
signals without letting Codex state control gameplay. `reputationMilestone`
is owned by the schema-v12 reputation system and must remain idempotent.

## World Events

- Filter immutable definitions by terrain, area, time, weather, level, quest
  state, boss state, prior outcomes, repeat limits, and cooldowns.
- Keep event chance independently capped at 8%; never feed it into or multiply
  the 15% random-encounter calculation.
- Persist the selected pending event before presenting choices or starting a
  special battle. Reload resumes the same choice or encounter.
- Apply skill outcomes through `rollSkillCheck()`, quest starts through
  `startQuestById()`, rewards through canonical item/XP helpers, and lore through
  `unlockCodexFromFutureSignal()`.
- Resolve stable outcome/reward IDs once, append at most 40 chronological
  records, and expose those records through Chronicle without revealing future
  choices.
- Alignment/reputation hooks are consumed by the centralized social mutation
  API with stable source IDs. World Event state never persists duplicate social
  scores or applied IDs.

## Alignment and reputation

- Keep canonical axes, faction IDs, reputation tiers, and thresholds in
  `src/data/reputation.ts`; reusable mechanics belong in
  `src/systems/reputation.ts`.
- New players begin exactly Chaotic Neutral (`lawChaos: -50`, `goodEvil: 0`).
- Persist only bounded scores, stable applied source IDs, and the bounded
  recent-cause history. Derive names, tiers, pricing, milestones, and ending
  variants.
- Apply social outcomes only for meaningful choices. Never reward routine
  movement, unavoidable combat, or farming.
- Return runtime-only `SocialAchievementHook` values for the achievement
  consumer; do not persist achievements inside the social system.

## Achievements

- Put immutable definitions and cosmetic titles in `src/data/achievements.ts`;
  put normalization, deterministic progress, reconciliation, stable event
  counters, debug exclusion, and title equip rules in
  `src/systems/achievements.ts`.
- Prefer reconciliation from authoritative quest, boss, Codex, exploration,
  trap, skill-check, event, social, party, and inventory state. Add persisted
  counters only for non-reconstructable event history such as battle wins,
  one-hit defeats, and explicit defeat count.
- Achievement state never controls gameplay authority. Titles are
  presentation-only and notices are queued for safe Overworld presentation.

## Adding spells, abilities, and equipment

- Damage sources may declare an `Element` from `src/data/elements.ts`.
- Player abilities may apply `selfEffect` or `targetEffect` IDs defined by
  `src/systems/statusEffects.ts`.
- Monster abilities use `statusEffect` for effects applied to the player.
- Cure consumables declare matching cure data and must be wired through
  `useItem()` without consuming the item when no matching ailment exists.
- Ally-target consumables declare `targetType`; resolve it through
  `getItemTargetType()` so older inventory copies use canonical item metadata.
- Preserve action economy: normal actions end the player turn; bonus-action
  abilities and the first item use do not.

Combat calculation order is:

1. Roll and resolve the attack or save.
2. Apply active-status accuracy, disadvantage, AC, and damage modifiers.
3. Apply elemental immunity, weakness, or resistance to the modified damage.
4. Apply damage and status effects.
5. Report discoveries and combat feedback.

Magic Missile remains auto-hit and does not roll disadvantage.

## Status effects

All definitions and lifecycle helpers live in
`src/systems/statusEffects.ts`. Do not duplicate status logic in data files or
scenes.

- Start of actor turn: tick damage, saving throws, and skip-turn decision.
- End of actor turn: decrement durations and expire effects.
- Apply or refresh through `applyStatusEffect()`.
- Normalize loaded effects through `normalizeActiveEffects()`.
- Clear player and monster effects when leaving Battle; durations are measured
  in combat turns, not overworld steps.

## Elements

Supported elements are Fire, Ice, Lightning, Poison, Necrotic, Radiant,
Thunder, Force, and Psychic.

- Immunity: zero damage
- Weakness: double damage
- Resistance: floor of half damage
- Neutral: unchanged

Record observed non-neutral interactions with `discoverElement()` so the Codex
can persist and display them.

## World features

- Cities may contain connected districts. Always use city chunk helpers rather
  than indexing `city.chunks` directly.
- Dungeons may contain multiple levels. Always use dungeon level and
  connection helpers.
- Dungeon trap layouts are derived from persisted `trapSeed`; never mutate
  dungeon maps or randomize layouts independently in scenes.
- Detected traps block movement until disarmed. Trap triggers must short-circuit
  the normal random-encounter check for that step.
- Use `FogOfWar.exploredKey()` for exploration keys.
- Use `isWalkable()` and `ENCOUNTER_RATES`; do not hardcode terrain behavior.
- Nautical metadata lives in `src/data/nautical.ts`; state normalization,
  ownership, and mechanics live in the focused `nauticalState.ts`,
  `nauticalOwnership.ts`, and `nautical.ts` modules. Preserve all 90 legacy
  chunk IDs and use `s:zoneId,chunkX,chunkY,x,y` for sea fog.
- Merchant routes work before boat ownership. Free sailing requires a
  serviceable active boat, uses canonical Water eligibility, and runs hazards
  before World Events, gathering, and random sea encounters.

## Non-combat skill checks

- Checks use d20 + Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier plus
  typed bonuses against a DC.
- Natural 1 and 20 are not automatic outcomes for ability checks.
- Persist fixed NPC, shop, chest, and treasure results in
  `player.progression.skillChecks`.
- Use stable NPC identities and shop type/coordinate keys rather than array
  indexes.
- Shop negotiation is one attempt per shop; successful discounts restore from
  the saved result.
- Exploration hazard damage is nonlethal and must clamp the player to at least
  1 HP.
- Test roll math, invalid inputs, stable data references, save normalization,
  reward bounds, and nonlethal damage deterministically.

## Scene changes

State-bearing transitions commonly pass:

```typescript
{
  player,
  defeatedBosses,
  codex,
  timeStep,
  weatherState,
  savedSpecialNpcs,
}
```

Battle also receives a `MonsterEncounter` and biome; Shop receives shop/city
context.
Defeat receives the full shared state plus encounter name/type and the exact
applied party defeat receipt. It must not recalculate or reapply penalties.
Future party systems pass accessor-backed `partyCombatants` plus runtime-only
`battleHooks`; do not persist those wrapper objects.
Keep target `init()` contracts and every caller synchronized.

The new-player tutorial opens only after pending opening cutscenes have drained.
`F1` and the Esc menu open the consultable Tips surface. Keep the external HTML
control rail collapsed by default and retain only contextual action prompts in
the game HUD.

Route camera fades and scene handoffs through
`src/managers/sceneTransition.ts`. Call `prepare()` when each scene creates,
wait for fade-complete events, and keep the duration-plus-grace watchdog as a
recovery path only. Restore the outgoing camera before queueing the next scene,
reject duplicate handoffs, and block state-changing Overworld input until the
queued start/restart is processed. Every Overworld restart must include a fresh
`savedSpecialNpcs` snapshot in the shared state payload.
Use the same guarded Battle exit cleanup for victory, flee, and defeat. Defeat
clears transient menus, input, effects, particles, and weather timers before
starting `DefeatScene`, which continues only to Overworld.
- Resolve an action before presenting it. Actor animation may read stable IDs,
  targets, hit/damage/healing, and outcome, but must not spend MP/items/actions,
  apply damage, report results, or control fade-complete scene handoffs.

## Companions and gambits

- Persistent party state lives at `player.party`; do not add a parallel scene
  payload or companion combat model.
- Stable companion IDs are `guardian`, `scout`, and `mystic`.
- Build runtime actors with `createPartyCombatant()` and
  `createBattleActionSource()`.
- Manual turns and ranked gambits both validate/execute through
  `battleActions.ts`; one bonus action may precede or follow one main action.
- Recruitment consumes replayable quest completion actions idempotently.
- Debug quest or companion recruitment must refresh live follower presentation
  immediately after replay.
- Active conscious companions may render as non-blocking followers, but only
  hero movement invokes trap, encounter, gate, and world-interaction logic.
- Keep party UI/followers/battle presentation in focused managers/renderers
  rather than growing the existing oversized scene/overlay files.

## Inventory presentation

- Build immutable views with `src/systems/inventory.ts`; every view entry keeps
  its original inventory index for actions and transfers.
- Never sort the owning inventory array or replace equipment object references.
- Keep sort/filter/search preferences in `2dnd_inventory_prefs`, outside the
  campaign save schema. Recent acquisition is reverse append order.
- Use semantic inventory actions for keyboard, pointer, gamepad, and touch
  controls. `T` remains mount control.
- Generate item visuals procedurally through `src/renderers/itemVisuals.ts`.

## Gathering

Gathering content lives in `src/data/gathering.ts`, deterministic node/table/
minigame logic in `src/systems/gathering.ts`, schema normalization in
`gatheringState.ts`, and accessible Phaser presentation in
`src/managers/gathering.ts`. Persist selected outcomes before play, use safe
location-derived nodes, route guarded finds through normal Battle hooks, and
keep material identity limited to stable `Item.material` recipe-input metadata.

## Crafting

Crafting recipes live in `src/data/crafting.ts`, atomic mechanics and discovery
in `src/systems/crafting.ts`, persistence normalization in `craftingState.ts`,
and accessible Overworld presentation in `src/managers/crafting.ts`. Validate
the selected actor inventory, protected/equipped restrictions, batch, gold,
station, output, and transaction ID before mutation. Equipment upgrades replace
exact equipped object links with canonical outputs. Never pull companion
materials implicitly, reroll a craft, duplicate material identity, or let
recipes/achievements control quests, Codex, access, or rewards.

## Validation

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:browser
npm run build
```

For UI changes, run the committed Playwright flow in headless Chromium. Keep
browser actions synchronized through debug-state transitions, and hold
frame-polled Phaser keys across frames rather than using instantaneous presses.
Build responsive UI from `src/systems/layout.ts`, register modal groups through
`createOverlayContainer()`, and assert the local `#layout-report` reports zero
unintended overlap or clipping at supported text scales.

## Common pitfalls

- Do not mutate shared monster, item, map, city, or dungeon definitions.
- Do not share HP, status, defend, discovery, or drop state between group
  combatants, including duplicate monsters.
- Do not introduce index-based turn entries or duplicate hero HP/effect state;
  use stable combatant IDs and `createHeroCombatant()`.
- Do not reimplement MP, inventory, target, formation, or action-economy checks
  in companion AI; use `validateBattleAction()`.
- Do not use stale Phaser 3 APIs or default imports; current code uses
  `import * as Phaser from "phaser"`.
- Do not create a second status or elemental calculation path.
- Do not omit unique dungeon pools or bosses from aggregate lookups.
- Do not use geometry masks for the Battle log; render the bounded visible
  message window.
- Do not add a persistent field without save normalization and tests.
- Do not reroll a failed trap detection; persist the `missed` state.

</skill-context>
I’m grounding the roadmap in the shipped architecture, current backlog, and active work.

1. # Agent guide
2. 
3. High-signal operating guide for changes to 2D&D. Read the relevant detailed
4. page in [`docs/`](docs/README.md) and matching
5. `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` before editing. Repository-wide constraints remain
6. authoritative in [`.github/copilot-instructions.md`](.github/copilot-instructions.md).
7. 
8. ## Snapshot
9. 
10. | Contract | Current value |
11. | --- | --- |
12. | Product | Browser JRPG, release v1.0.0 |
13. | Runtime | Phaser 4.2.1 |
14. | Language | TypeScript 7.0.2, strict, ES2020 |
15. | Build/test | Vite 8.2.1, Vitest 4.1.10, Playwright 1.62.1 |
16. | DOM tests | happy-dom 20.11.1 |
17. | Save schema | 17 |
18. | Deployment | GitHub Pages at `/2dnd/` |
19. | Assets | Procedural graphics and Web Audio only |
20. 
21. Only current `main` is shipped behavior. Treat issues and open pull requests as
22. future work until merged.
23. 
24. ## Task routing
25. 
26. | Domain | Data/contracts | Mechanics/state | Phaser/presentation | Tests |
27. | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
28. | Combat/status/elements | `src/data/{abilities,spells,elements}.ts` | `src/systems/{combat,groupCombat,battleActions,statusEffects}.ts` | `Battle.ts`, battle managers/renderers | `combat`, `groupCombat`, `battleActions`, `statusEffects`, Battle E2E |
29. | Party/gambits/inventory | `src/data/companions.ts` | `party.ts`, `gambits.ts`, `inventory.ts` | `partyOverlay.ts`, `battleParty.ts`, followers/renderers | party/companion/gambit/inventory suites |
30. | Quests/cutscenes | `quests.ts`, focused `cutscene*.ts` | `quests.ts`, `questState.ts`, `cutscenes.ts` | quest/cutscene managers, `Cutscene.ts`, `Ending.ts` | quest/cutscene/campaign E2E |
31. | World/map/traps | `map*.ts`, `chunks.ts`, `cities.ts`, `dungeons.ts`, `traps.ts` | `movement.ts`, `traps.ts` | map/city/trap/fog managers/renderers | map, city, trap, fog, movement |
32. | Sea navigation | `nautical.ts`, `islands.ts`, `seaMonsters.ts` | `nautical*.ts` | Overworld/map/audio | nautical unit and E2E |
33. | Events/social/achievements | matching `src/data/` modules | matching `src/systems/` modules | managers/overlays/social renderer | matching unit and E2E |
34. | Gathering/crafting | matching `src/data/` modules | matching systems + state normalizers | matching managers | matching unit and E2E |
35. | Saves | owning interfaces/defaults | `save.ts` plus focused state normalizers | Boot/load/recovery callers | `save.test.ts` + domain migration tests |
36. | Accessibility/input | tutorial/feature definitions | `accessibility.ts`, `input.ts`, `featureDiscovery.ts` | input/tutorial/layout managers | accessibility/input/layout/feature E2E |
37. | Audio | typed data cues | `audio.ts`, `trapAudio.ts` | callers only | audio + representative browser flows |
38. | UI/layout | stable IDs/content definitions | `systems/layout.ts` | `managers/layout.ts`, owning manager/renderer | layout unit + clean-layout E2E |
39. 
40. ## Required workflow
41. 
42. 1. **Inspect:** check current branch/base, related data/system/manager/renderer,
43.    callers, tests, docs, skills, and merged history. Search for an existing
44.    helper before creating one.
45. 2. **Implement:** change the authoritative layer first, then adapters and
46.    presentation. Keep IDs stable and edits focused.
47. 3. **Targeted validate:** run the smallest related Vitest files and focused
48.    Playwright specs.
49. 4. **Full gate:** run install/audit, typecheck, full Vitest, full Playwright,
50.    build, and `git diff --check`.
51. 5. **PR/CI:** push a review branch, open a PR, wait for PR CI and CodeQL, and
52.    resolve every failure and review comment. Do not merge without explicit
53.    instruction.
54. 
55. ```bash
56. npm ci
57. npm audit
58. npm run typecheck
59. npm test
60. npm run test:browser
61. npm run build
62. git diff --check
63. ```
64. 
65. Run `npm run test:browser:install` once when Chromium is absent.
66. 
67. ## Non-negotiable invariants
68. 
69. - Strict TypeScript, explicit types, no `any`, no unsafe nested save casts.
70. - No external image/audio assets, gameplay network calls, or runtime mutation
71.   of shared definitions.
72. - Build scene payloads with `createSharedSceneState()`; preserve player, bosses,
73.   Codex, time, weather, and special NPCs.
74. - `SceneTransitionManager` owns fades. Fade-complete is authoritative; the
75.   duration-plus-grace timer is recovery only.
76. - `battleActions.ts` owns party action validation, targets, resources, and
77.   one-action/one-bonus-action economy.
78. - Resolve mechanics before animation; presentation never spends resources or
79.   controls authoritative outcomes.
80. - Use stable IDs for combatants, quests/stages/objectives/rewards, cutscenes,
81.   shops, traps, events, recipes, transactions, features, and layout items.
82. - Persist authority, not derived presentation. Every schema change requires
83.   defaults, normalization, cross-field validation, migration, and corruption
84.   tests.
85. - Route all release input through semantic contexts; do not add scene-local
86.   gamepad/touch mappings or conflicting production/debug keys.
87. - Own and clean up listeners, timers, tweens, emitters, DOM controls, texture
88.   leases, and transient containers.
89. - Install accessibility in every scene; support text scales, high contrast,
90.   reduced motion, non-color cues, touch, and gamepad cursor flows.
91. - Use `debugLog()`/debug panels, never production `console.log`.
92. - At 1,000 source lines, consider extraction before adding responsibility.
93. 
94. ## Frequent regressions and the correct pattern
95. 
96. | Pitfall | Correct pattern |
97. | --- | --- |
98. | Fixed UI coordinates or raw menu indexes | Stable layout IDs, measured bounds, filtered entries, focus restoration |
99. | Timer-driven scene start | Fade-complete listener plus delayed recovery watchdog |
100. | Partial scene payload | `createSharedSceneState()` and update every caller/test |
101. | New field without migration | Interface + default + unknown normalization + cross-field repair + schema bump + tests |
102. | Duplicate combat logic in scene/AI | Plan and execute through `battleActions.ts` and existing combat/status/element helpers |
103. | Keyboard fix that breaks touch/gamepad | Semantic action/context in system layer, browser adapter in `managers/input.ts` |
104. | Browser test on stale server/root path | `npm run test:browser`; fresh strict port and `/2dnd/` default |
105. | Docs copied from an issue or branch | Verify current `main`, source constants, package manifest, and merged PR |
106. | Parallel features merged in arbitrary order | Identify shared files, choose dependency order, rebase after prerequisite, preserve both contracts |
107. | Targeted tests only | Full typecheck, Vitest, Playwright, build, audit, CI, and CodeQL before completion |
108. | Growing scenes/overlays | Extract focused system, manager, renderer, or data module |
109. 
110. ## Change checklists
111. 
112. ### Persistence
113. 
114. - [ ] Owning interface and creation default updated
115. - [ ] Parsed value treated as `unknown`
116. - [ ] IDs, ranges, duplicates, and cross-fields normalized
117. - [ ] `SAVE_VERSION` incremented for shape changes
118. - [ ] Deterministic pending state cannot reroll or double-apply
119. - [ ] Legacy and corrupt data tests added
120. - [ ] README/docs/instructions/save skill synchronized
121. 
122. ### Scene
123. 
124. - [ ] `init()` stores input and resets transient state
125. - [ ] `create()` calls transition preparation and accessibility installation
126. - [ ] Every caller passes the complete typed contract
127. - [ ] Input is blocked while handoff is pending
128. - [ ] Listeners/timers/tweens/emitters/DOM/textures cleaned on shutdown
129. - [ ] Reduced motion completes immediately and exactly once
130. - [ ] Transition contract and browser flow covered
131. 
132. ### UI/layout
133. 
134. - [ ] Hidden/disabled entries filtered before layout
135. - [ ] Stable item/layout IDs used
136. - [ ] Actual scaled bounds and safe areas measured
137. - [ ] Hit areas synchronized after reflow
138. - [ ] Focus restored by ID and clamped
139. - [ ] Keyboard, pointer, touch, gamepad, 150% text, high contrast, and reduced motion checked
140. - [ ] Layout audit reports no unintended overlap or clipping
141. 
142. ### Combat
143. 
144. - [ ] Stable combatant/target IDs used
145. - [ ] Existing target/resource/action-economy validator reused
146. - [ ] MP/items/actions consumed only after validation
147. - [ ] Status then element ordering preserved
148. - [ ] Duplicate monsters retain independent state and defeat records
149. - [ ] Mechanics resolve before animation
150. - [ ] Victory/flee/defeat report once and share guarded cleanup
151. 
152. ### Integration and conflicts
153. 
154. - [ ] Confirm prerequisite merge order before combining cross-cutting work

{"body":"## Focused v2 roadmap

This epic tracks post-campaign-release work. Every remaining capability now has a focused issue with explicit scope, dependencies, migration, accessibility, testing, and release requirements.

## Phase 1: Platform and state foundations

- [ ] Secure Electron desktop packaging and cross-platform artifacts (#162)
- [ ] Multiple save slots and storage recovery (#166)
- [ ] Data-driven difficulty modes and custom rules (#171)

## Phase 2: Battle presentation and optional pressure

- [ ] Visible authoritative dice presentation (#165)
- [ ] Optional timed-round battle mode (#164)

## Phase 3: Additional activities and character progression

- [ ] Tavern and festival challenge minigames (#167)
- [ ] Hero multiclass progression (#168)
- [ ] Optional fictional religion and devotion (#169)
- [ ] Prestige-class progression paths (#170), after #168 and with optional #169 prerequisites

## Phase 4: Replay and epic progression

- [ ] New Game Plus and epic-level progression (#172), after #166 and #171

## Final release gate

- [ ] Integrated v2 release and migration matrix (#173)

## Already delivered

- [x] Gambit system with auto-battle control
- [x] Side quests and the full Twelvefold Covenant campaign
- [x] Campaign cutscenes and ending (#140, #141)
- [x] Mobile and gamepad semantic controls (#89)
- [x] v1 roadmap and post-release depth through sea navigation (#73)

## Delivery rules

- Work from the current default branch; do not stack unless explicitly requested.
- Preserve browser behavior while expanding Electron coverage.
- Treat save migration, normalization, corruption recovery, accessibility, semantic controls, docs, and full browser/desktop validation as part of every persistent or UI feature.
- Keep Standard/default behavior regression-compatible unless a focused issue explicitly changes it.
- The final gate must pass before a v2 release is considered ready.

# 171 Add data-driven difficulty modes and custom rules
## Goal

Add selectable difficulty modes through centralized rules while preserving the current game exactly as Standard.

## Scope

- Define Story, Standard, Veteran, and Legendary modes plus a constrained Custom profile using typed, bounded modifiers.
- Centralize modifiers for enemy HP/damage/accuracy/AI, encounter pressure, flee DC, non-combat skill-check assistance, defeat penalties, economy/rewards, recovery, and optional timed-round integration.
- Keep Standard values identical to current `main`; prohibit scattered scene-level difficulty conditionals.
- Decide and surface which settings can change mid-campaign. Changes must be explicit, logged in save metadata, and never silently alter achievement eligibility.
- Add new-game selection, save-slot metadata, settings/character-sheet explanation, clear effect previews, and adaptive Tutorial/Tips guidance.
- Support accessibility independently: high contrast, reduced motion, text scaling, input method, and dice presentation must never change mechanical difficulty.
- Integrate achievements and New Game+ extension points without implementing NG+ here.
- Ensure bosses, groups, companions/gambits, sea encounters, hazards, events, gathering, crafting economy, alignment/reputation, and campaign ending remain valid at every mode.
- Persist only the selected profile and bounded custom overrides; derive all rule values from canonical definitions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Standard mode is mechanically regression-identical to the existing game.
- Every modifier flows through shared helpers and is visible to tests/debug explanations.
- No mode creates impossible campaign gates, negative rewards, uncapped encounter rates, or invalid save state.
- Accessibility preferences do not affect achievement/difficulty classification.
- Changing allowed settings cannot duplicate battle/event/quest outcomes or reapply rewards.

## Validation

- Snapshot/invariant tests comparing Standard to baseline and boundary tests for every modifier/profile.
- Full campaign, boss, economy, event, sea, skill-check, defeat/recovery, save migration, and achievement-eligibility tests per mode.
- Playwright coverage for new-game selection, custom rules, save metadata, mid-run policy, mobile/gamepad, and completion on representative modes.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

# 172 Add New Game Plus and epic-level progression
## Goal

Add replayable New Game+ campaigns and level 21-30 epic progression without mutating the completed source campaign.

## Dependencies

- Multiple save slots and atomic copy semantics (#166).
- Data-driven difficulty profiles (#171).
- Multiclass/prestige systems should expose compatible progression APIs when present (#168, #170), but NG+ must also support single-class heroes.

## Scope

- Unlock New Game+ only from an authoritative completed campaign and create it as a new save slot/cycle.
- Define explicit carry/reset policy for hero/companions, levels, equipment, inventory/materials, gold, titles/achievements, Codex/lore, recipes/gathering, boat, cosmetics, alignment/reputation/devotion, quests, bosses, world discovery, cutscenes, events, chests, and one-shot rewards.
- Never overwrite or mutate the source completed slot.
- Add cycle number and stable NG+ metadata, deterministic reset/reconciliation, and corruption recovery.
- Add level 21-30 epic XP curves, HP/MP/stat/proficiency rules, ASIs/talents or epic boons, multiclass/prestige compatibility, and bounded progression.
- Scale enemies, bosses, groups, encounters, sea zones, rewards, shops, crafting, and events through centralized NG+/difficulty helpers, not mutated shared data.
- Add NG+-specific optional variants, drops, achievements, Codex entries, events, and post-game challenges while preserving the canonical campaign sequence and ending.
- Prevent repeated one-shot rewards, quest completion actions, companion recruitment, achievements, or carried equipment links from duplicating.
- Add title/new-game/save-slot UI, carry-policy preview, confirmation, cycle summary, and Tutorial/Tips updates with full accessibility/input support.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting NG+ creates an independent valid slot and leaves the original campaign byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Every persisted subsystem has a documented, tested carry/reset rule.
- The campaign remains completable through the real final interaction on every supported cycle/difficulty.
- Epic levels compose with single-class, multiclass, and prestige progression without exceeding defined caps or double-granting features.
- Reload, migration, and repeated NG+ creation are deterministic and idempotent.

## Validation

- Complete carry/reset matrix, source-slot immutability, reward idempotency, epic progression, scaling, migration/corruption, and multi-cycle tests.
- Full browser/Electron golden paths from completed save to NG+ ending, including touch/gamepad, accessibility, defeat, sea, crafting, achievements, and save-slot recovery.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

# 173 Validate the integrated v2 release and migration matrix
## Goal

# 171 Add data-driven difficulty modes and custom rules
## Goal

Add selectable difficulty modes through centralized rules while preserving the current game exactly as Standard.

## Scope

- Define Story, Standard, Veteran, and Legendary modes plus a constrained Custom profile using typed, bounded modifiers.
- Centralize modifiers for enemy HP/damage/accuracy/AI, encounter pressure, flee DC, non-combat skill-check assistance, defeat penalties, economy/rewards, recovery, and optional timed-round integration.
- Keep Standard values identical to current `main`; prohibit scattered scene-level difficulty conditionals.
- Decide and surface which settings can change mid-campaign. Changes must be explicit, logged in save metadata, and never silently alter achievement eligibility.
- Add new-game selection, save-slot metadata, settings/character-sheet explanation, clear effect previews, and adaptive Tutorial/Tips guidance.
- Support accessibility independently: high contrast, reduced motion, text scaling, input method, and dice presentation must never change mechanical difficulty.
- Integrate achievements and New Game+ extension points without implementing NG+ here.
- Ensure bosses, groups, companions/gambits, sea encounters, hazards, events, gathering, crafting economy, alignment/reputation, and campaign ending remain valid at every mode.
- Persist only the selected profile and bounded custom overrides; derive all rule values from canonical definitions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Standard mode is mechanically regression-identical to the existing game.
- Every modifier flows through shared helpers and is visible to tests/debug explanations.
- No mode creates impossible campaign gates, negative rewards, uncapped encounter rates, or invalid save state.
- Accessibility preferences do not affect achievement/difficulty classification.
- Changing allowed settings cannot duplicate battle/event/quest outcomes or reapply rewards.

## Validation

- Snapshot/invariant tests comparing Standard to baseline and boundary tests for every modifier/profile.
- Full campaign, boss, economy, event, sea, skill-check, defeat/recovery, save migration, and achievement-eligibility tests per mode.
- Playwright coverage for new-game selection, custom rules, save metadata, mid-run policy, mobile/gamepad, and completion on representative modes.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

## Goal

Add replayable New Game+ campaigns and level 21-30 epic progression without mutating the completed source campaign.

## Dependencies

- Multiple save slots and atomic copy semantics (#166).
- Data-driven difficulty profiles (#171).
- Multiclass/prestige systems should expose compatible progression APIs when present (#168, #170), but NG+ must also support single-class heroes.

## Scope

- Unlock New Game+ only from an authoritative completed campaign and create it as a new save slot/cycle.
- Define explicit carry/reset policy for hero/companions, levels, equipment, inventory/materials, gold, titles/achievements, Codex/lore, recipes/gathering, boat, cosmetics, alignment/reputation/devotion, quests, bosses, world discovery, cutscenes, events, chests, and one-shot rewards.
- Never overwrite or mutate the source completed slot.
- Add cycle number and stable NG+ metadata, deterministic reset/reconciliation, and corruption recovery.
- Add level 21-30 epic XP curves, HP/MP/stat/proficiency rules, ASIs/talents or epic boons, multiclass/prestige compatibility, and bounded progression.
- Scale enemies, bosses, groups, encounters, sea zones, rewards, shops, crafting, and events through centralized NG+/difficulty helpers, not mutated shared data.
- Add NG+-specific optional variants, drops, achievements, Codex entries, events, and post-game challenges while preserving the canonical campaign sequence and ending.
- Prevent repeated one-shot rewards, quest completion actions, companion recruitment, achievements, or carried equipment links from duplicating.
- Add title/new-game/save-slot UI, carry-policy preview, confirmation, cycle summary, and Tutorial/Tips updates with full accessibility/input support.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting NG+ creates an independent valid slot and leaves the original campaign byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Every persisted subsystem has a documented, tested carry/reset rule.
- The campaign remains completable through the real final interaction on every supported cycle/difficulty.
- Epic levels compose with single-class, multiclass, and prestige progression without exceeding defined caps or double-granting features.
- Reload, migration, and repeated NG+ creation are deterministic and idempotent.

## Validation

- Complete carry/reset matrix, source-slot immutability, reward idempotency, epic progression, scaling, migration/corruption, and multi-cycle tests.
- Full browser/Electron golden paths from completed save to NG+ ending, including touch/gamepad, accessibility, defeat, sea, crafting, achievements, and save-slot recovery.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

# 167 Add tavern and festival challenge minigames
## Goal

Add replayable social and skill-based minigames beyond resource gathering, using existing world, economy, event, social, and achievement systems.

## Scope

Implement three distinct data-driven activities:

- **Crown & Bones:** an original push-your-luck tavern dice game using in-game gold only, with transparent odds and capped stakes.
- **Archery Challenge:** a timing/precision range available at selected cities and festivals, with class-neutral scoring.
- **Harbor Regatta:** a route/obstacle sailing challenge using the nautical movement model, boat condition, weather, and semantic controls.

For each activity:

- Define stable activity, venue, ruleset, difficulty, score, reward, and record IDs.
- Add simple interactive mechanics with deterministic seeded challenge layouts and reduced-motion alternatives.
- Integrate city/faction reputation, random events, Codex lore, achievements, and balanced rewards without making minigame state authoritative for quests.
- Prevent guaranteed buy-in/reward arbitrage, repeated-input duplication, debug achievement leakage, and reload rerolls.
- Persist personal bests, bounded history, once-only rewards, and pending sessions only where needed for crash-safe recovery.
- Add accessible venue discovery, instructions, leaderboards/personal records, adaptive prompts, keyboard/pointer/touch/gamepad, mobile safe areas, high contrast, and text scaling.
- Reuse shared dice presentation when available but keep authoritative minigame resolution independent of animation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every activity has distinct mechanics, rewards, venues, progression, and deterministic tests.
- Losing or abandoning an activity cannot corrupt gold, reputation, boat state, input contexts, or scene transitions.
- Stakes and rewards use in-game currency only; no real-money, network, or gambling-service integration exists.
- Existing campaign completion remains optional and unaffected.

## Validation

- Unit tests for rules, seeded layouts, scoring, reward caps, economy anti-arbitrage, pending recovery, social/achievement hooks, and cleanup.
- Browser/Electron Playwright coverage for all activities using keyboard, touch, and gamepad, including reduced motion and reload recovery.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

# 168 Add hero multiclass progression
## Goal

Allow the hero to combine multiple existing classes through a typed D&D-inspired progression model without invalidating single-class characters or companions.

## Scope

- Replace the hero's single-class level ownership with stable per-class levels plus total character level, while preserving the original starting class identity.
- Keep proficiency based on total level; derive HP, MP, hit-die growth, class features, spells, abilities, talents, ASIs, equipment permissions, and primary-stat behavior from explicit multiclass rules.
- Define data-driven entry prerequisites and feature-grant levels for all 12 current classes.
- Cap normal progression at total level 20; do not implement epic levels in this issue.
- Keep companions single-class unless separately designed later.
- Add level-up UI for selecting the next class, previewing gained features/resources, allocating stats, and explaining unmet prerequisites.
- Resolve overlapping spells/abilities, action economy, known-action normalization, class-specific resources, equipment, and save/load deterministically.
- Preserve existing single-class saves exactly through migration and ensure single-class level-ups behave as before.
- Integrate shops, quests, dialogue, Codex, achievements, gambits, manual companion combat, character sheet, and debug commands without making multiclass state authoritative for campaign progression.
- Do not add unrestricted respec; any future respec requires a separate balance design.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every legal class combination remains type-safe, loadable, and playable through battle and level-up.
- Total-level caps, prerequisites, HP/MP growth, proficiency, ASIs, known actions, and equipment links cannot be double-applied.
- Existing level-1 through level-20 single-class saves migrate without lost stats, spells, abilities, talents, or equipment.
- Character creation still selects one starting class and remains unchanged unless multiclassing is explicitly chosen later.

## Validation

- Deterministic tests for all class entry requirements, feature tables, total/per-class levels, HP/MP/ASI progression, overlaps, save migration, corruption, gambits, and battle execution.
- Playwright coverage for several martial/caster/hybrid combinations, level-up previews, save/reload, equipment, mobile/gamepad, and campaign completion.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

# 169 Add an optional fictional religion and devotion system
## Goal

Add an original in-world pantheon, devotion choices, temples, and optional blessings that deepen roleplay without using real-world religions or creating campaign softlocks.

## Scope

- Define a fully fictional pantheon with stable deity, domain, tenet, temple, rite, blessing, quest, dialogue, and devotion-source IDs.
- Let players remain unaffiliated, follow one deity, or change affiliation through explicit in-world choices with documented consequences.
- Track bounded devotion separately from alignment and faction/town reputation; centralized idempotent sources must prevent repeated quest/dialogue/event application.
- Integrate temples, prayers/rites, NPC dialogue, Codex lore, random events, quests, sea/island content, alignment/reputation, achievements, and ending presentation.
- Add optional temporary or cosmetic blessings through existing status/item/rest APIs; no deity may be required for campaign completion or provide an overwhelmingly optimal combat path.
- Use alignment as context, not a hard one-to-one lock. Conflicting choices may affect devotion through explicit data-driven rules.
- Add accessible character/profile and temple surfaces showing affiliation, domains, tenets, devotion tier/progress, active blessing, recent causes, and available rites.
- Support keyboard/pointer/touch/gamepad, text scaling, high contrast, reduced motion, and non-color cues.
- Add stable extension points for prestige-class prerequisites without implementing prestige classes here.
- Preserve unaffiliated legacy saves through migration and avoid retroactively inferring devotion from historical choices unless reconstruction is safe and explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

- All content is original and fictional; no real religion, scripture, ritual, or living belief system is represented.
- Devotion, alignment, and reputation remain distinct authoritative states.
- Repeated interactions, reloads, debug commands, and quest replay cannot duplicate devotion or blessings.
- Every affiliation choice and an unaffiliated run can complete the full campaign.
- Blessings expire, save, load, and clean up through existing lifecycle rules.

## Validation

- Data-integrity, source-idempotency, affiliation/change, devotion-tier, blessing, social interaction, migration/corruption, and authority-isolation tests.
- Playwright coverage for unaffiliated and affiliated paths, temple UI, blessings, dialogue/event consequences, ending presentation, touch/gamepad, and accessibility.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.

# 170 Add prestige-class progression paths
## Goal

Add advanced optional progression paths that build on hero multiclassing and world choices without replacing base-class identity.

## Dependencies

- Hero multiclass progression must land first (#168).
- Religion/devotion may provide optional prerequisites for selected paths (#169), but unaffiliated prestige options must exist.

## Scope

- Define original prestige paths with stable IDs, prerequisites, levels, feature tables, abilities/spells/talents, equipment rules, lore, and unlock sources.
- Provide a balanced launch set spanning martial, arcane, divine, primal, stealth, and hybrid archetypes; avoid names or content copied from published tabletop subclasses.
- Enter prestige progression only after explicit total-level, class-level, stat, quest, achievement, alignment/reputation, Codex, or devotion requirements.
- Prestige levels count toward the normal total-level cap and use the multiclass progression engine; they must not double proficiency, ASIs, HP/MP, or action economy.
- Keep every prestige path optional and ensure normal classes can complete all campaign/post-game content.
- Add preview/qualification UI, character-sheet presentation, Tips/Codex lore, achievements, and debug inspection.
- Define deterministic behavior when a later social/devotion change no longer matches an entry prerequisite: earned levels remain valid unless an explicit suspension rule is safely designed and surfaced.
- Preserve non-prestige saves through migration without retroactive unlock mutation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every path has valid, test-covered prerequisites and a complete progression table.
- Invalid entry, repeated level-up input, save reload, or debug mutation cannot duplicate features or resources.
- Base/multiclass/prestige levels compose through one typed progression engine.
- No prestige path is mandatory or strictly dominates comparable base progression.
- Gambits, equipment, combat actions, shops, saves, achievements, and Ending summaries support prestige heroes.

## Validation

- Exhaustive prerequisite, progression, feature-overlap, balance-invariant, migration, corruption, level-cap, and action-execution tests.
- Playwright coverage for qualification, rejection, multiple archetypes, level-up, save/reload, battle, mobile/gamepad, and campaign completion.
- Full typecheck, Vitest, browser/Electron suites, builds, audit, and CI/CodeQL.
